summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — ALLE +11%, ROP +10%, LEN +8%, BX +8%, HPQ +8%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (MRNA -18%, COHR -13%, LRCX -12%, LITE -12%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: MRNA (-17.93%) — Sell-the-news after leaked Phase 3 melanoma data (intismeran + Keytruda, 42% lower recurrence risk) ahead of ESMO. Shares had roughly quadrupled since August, and Citi downgraded on valuation. Search dates the main drop to Oct 22. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: a mid/large-cap biotech that is not in any momentum or mean-reversion list. It was also a news-leak gap-down on a stock up about 4x in two months, and a long-only bot cannot short it.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 earnings beat: adjusted EPS $2.60 vs ~$2.48 consensus, revenue $1.17B (+9.6%, +7.2% organic) vs ~$1.13B est., and the full-year 2026 outlook was raised.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ALLE is a mid-cap industrial (security hardware) that no strategy covers. It was also an earnings gap, so the move came on the open and a post-open momentum signal would have been late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-gap scan: admit any US name with a gap of at least +5%, EPS and revenue beats, and a guidance raise to the momentum strategy's universe for that session, bypassing the static universe list.

top_movers.catalyst: Follow-through from Q3 results reported 10/22: adj EPS $5.89 beat the $5.79 estimate, revenue rose 8%, and FY EPS guidance was raised to $22.35-22.40. No separate 10/23 news found, so the +10% is likely a delayed re-rating.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ROP is a ~$45B mid/large-cap software and industrial-tech compounder that no strategy lists. The stock was flat premarket on 10/22, so a gap-based or earnings-day trigger would not have fired.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-drift scanner that admits any S&P 500 name into the momentum universe when the 1-day move is ≥ +7% within 2 sessions of an earnings beat plus guidance raise, even if it is not in a static universe list.

top_movers.catalyst: Rate-driven homebuilder rally: the 10-yr Treasury yield fell below 5% and mortgage rates eased, on top of Berkshire Hathaway's reported ~11% LEN stake build. No company-specific news found.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LEN is a large-cap homebuilder, and no strategy covers housing or rate-sensitive cyclicals. The move was a macro and rates sector move, with no earnings gap or news-reactive signal to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a rate-sensitive sector basket (LEN, DHI, PHM, ITB) to the momentum universe, gated on a ≥10bp one-day drop in the 10-yr yield plus ≥+3% sector-ETF move, so the next rate-relief rally is caught.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings: distributable EPS $1.32 beat the $1.29 estimate, credit/insurance inflows were $35.8B, AUM hit $1.37T and credit DE turned up. Premarket was +3.4%; the session closed up 8.2%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BX is a large-cap alternative asset manager/financial that no strategy lists. The move was an earnings-gap catalyst, so a post-open momentum or news bot would also have found the gap already priced.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap financials/alt managers (BX, KKR, APO) to the news-reactive universe, and release the earnings gate for names that beat EPS and gap up ≥3% premarket, entering within the first 30 minutes after the open.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed company-specific news found. The move looks like a rally in AI PC / workstation hardware names, with HPE and Dell also up on the day, rather than an earnings or M&A event.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HPQ is a mid-cap PC/printer hardware name that no strategy lists. With no pre-market news catalyst, a news-reactive bot had nothing to trigger on, and a momentum screen would only see the gap at the open.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'unlisted movers' scan to the momentum-trader's candidate set: any US stock above $5B market cap with a gap ≥ +5% and volume ≥ 1.5× its 20-day average gets added to the universe for that session.

top_movers.catalyst: No GIS-specific news found. It looks like a continuing staples/defensive rally after P&G's earnings beat sparked +6-8% moves on Oct 22, extending a bounce from a ~30% drawdown.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. GIS is a large-cap, low-beta packaged-food staple, and the universe likely favours growth, tech or high-beta names. The move was sector-driven with no stock-specific trigger, and it started a day earlier.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a consumer-staples sector-momentum rule: if ≥3 staples names gain ≥4% on volume ≥1.5× the 20-day average after a bellwether earnings beat (e.g. PG), let a defensive sleeve enter the laggards on day 2.

top_movers.catalyst: Sell-the-news after leaked Phase 3 melanoma data (intismeran + Keytruda, 42% lower recurrence risk) ahead of ESMO. Shares had roughly quadrupled since August, and Citi downgraded on valuation. Search dates the main drop to Oct 22.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: a mid/large-cap biotech that is not in any momentum or mean-reversion list. It was also a news-leak gap-down on a stock up about 4x in two months, and a long-only bot cannot short it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-gap 'parabolic-run exhaustion' watchlist: biotechs with a >150% 60-day gain and a >10% single-day drop would feed the mean-reversion universe, so a bounce entry is considered after day 2 once volume normalizes.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide AI optics selloff, with COHR down about 12% and Lumentum also lower, reported as AI optics stocks cooling ahead of earnings. I found no company-specific news. The date attribution is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: COHR is a mid/large-cap photonics name that no strategy's universe includes. The drop was a high-beta sector de-rating with no single catalyst for a news-reactive bot to key on, and the bot likely has no short capability.
top_movers.suggestion: Add AI-optics/semis names (COHR, LITE, AAOI) to the mean-reversion universe, with a sector-wide gate that fires when ≥3 peers fall ≥7% on the same day. Only then consider a rebound entry, with a size cap.

top_movers.catalyst: Lam's Dec-quarter guide (~$8.6B, barely above consensus) cited supply-chain constraints that could push shipments into March. That set off a chip-wide selloff (SOX -6.7%) amid AI-capex doubts.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LRCX is a large-cap semiconductor-equipment name that no strategy lists. The drop was an earnings-reaction gap (results were after the close on 10/21), so a post-print gap-down was already priced at the open.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap semi-equipment names (LRCX, AMAT, KLAC) to the news-reactive universe. Also add a sector-contagion rule that flags names when SOX falls more than 4% on a day with a bellwether earnings gap.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued AI-optics sector selloff (Coherent, AAOI, Ciena, Lumentum) on tech weakness and AI-capex worries ahead of earnings. I found no company-specific news. Sources only confirm the Oct 22 leg, not Oct 23.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LITE is a high-priced (~$750), highly volatile mid/large-cap optical-networking name after a ~500% run, so it likely fails the universe's price/volatility screens. The drop was a sector-wide move, not a catalyst the news filter could act on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'high-beta AI-hardware' sub-universe (LITE, COHR, CIEN, AAOI) with a sector-relative mean-reversion rule, e.g. consider entry when the basket falls ≥8% in 2 days with no company-specific news.
